page.text:
An action turns structural questions into counting and geometry. A
transitive action has a single orbit and presents $X$ as a coset space.
Conjugation of $G$ on itself has conjugacy classes as orbits and
centralizers as stabilizers. These examples explain why quotient groups
and actions are not separate topics but two views of the same symmetry
mechanism.
